reviews.title: It had potential
reviews.text:
For a few months it worked pretty well. However, during the past two months I have not been able to access my saved palettes. It just shows the loading wheel, but nothing shows up. 
I wish it would do what it says it should because as of right now it is not worth the paid subscription.

reviews.title: Price gouging at its finest
reviews.text:
This is a great tool, don't get me wrong! I love it so much and do use it fairly often. But this subscription model is absolutely ridiculous and exploitative.

I've used the app for a long time; "pro" features were a one time purchase back then; not super cheap upfront but worth it over time. A subscription is maybe understandable for an indispensable, widely featured, and always evolving app. But this isn't that. It's a color picker, with comparable free options, and nothing has changed except minor interface tweaks and optimization for over 5 years. One well paid dev can clock in for like 5 hours a year and do more than this company has. The free version is basically useless; there are better places to find existing palettes, which is all it offers. I only use the app at all because they still honor the one time purchase I made, but I would strongly recommend against it unless you're one of the few designers who don't mind paying a ransom for basic tools.

If you're a big corporation's design lead, this is great. But it's a terrible use of money for students, hobbyists, nonprofit designers, rural companies, independent businesses, etc etc etc. (there are no discounts or exceptions currently)

I have books with extensive details on color theory, huge pallette collections, and helpful tailored advice; none of which cost more than 2 months of this app.

reviews.title: Rug pull
reviews.text: I paid for this app and then it became subscription based. I do not support that business model and I think it’s laughable it still says “made with love” after doing that. The app itself does not provide enough value to be a subscription.
